subject: Encryption evidence request & sanitized KMS/HSM extracts
messages:
From: Tom Weaver <tom.weaver@aurorafinance.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 8 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Request: encryption + KMS/HSM evidence for SIG/CAIQ sections

Alex —

As part of Aurora's SIG review for our production integration, we need a concise package that covers key management and cryptography controls. Can you please provide the following by EOD next Wednesday (2025-07-16)?

- HSM attestation or vendor certificate (most recent)
- KMS key rotation logs (sanitized): last 12 months, include timestamps, actor id (pseudonym ok), key IDs (hashed OK)
- Description of at-rest encryption (envelope/wrapping details) and transit TLS configuration
- Short statement on split-key/escrow practices (if any) and emergency rotation runbook summary

We're fine with redacted/sanitized extracts as long as timestamps and rotation events are preserved. If you have a pre-built CAIQ/SIG pack for crypto controls, that would be ideal.

Also confirm any restrictions on sharing key material or raw PKCS#11 traces — we do not need raw material, just attestations and audit traces.

Thanks,
Tom
Security Engineer
Aurora Finance
security@aurorafinance.com

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 8 Jul 2025 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: Fwd: Request: encryption + KMS/HSM evidence for SIG/CAIQ sections

Irene / Marissa — forwarding Aurora's request. Short plan below; please reply with what you can attach and a target for delivery.

Action items:
- Irene: pull the most recent HSM attestation and vendor sign-off (we typically have the vendor PDF). Prep a one-paragraph summary describing the attestation scope (tenant separation, key lifecycle). Mark any PII in attachments for redaction.
- Marissa: export rotation events from the KMS for the past 12 months. Per Tom, we can pseudonymize actor IDs and hash key identifiers. Produce a CSV with columns: event_ts, key_id_hash, rotation_type, actor_hash, notes. Add a short redaction_notes.txt describing what was modified.
- Alex (me): prepare a short CAIQ/SIG snippet describing envelope encryption, wrapping KEKs, transit TLS config (cipher suites, TLS version), and the emergency rotation runbook summary. I'll assemble the package into a single PDF for delivery and include the Drive link.

Constraints to keep in mind: do not include raw private keys or PKCS#11 dumps. For HSM vendor attestations, check whether the PDF contains cryptographic material that needs redaction — if so, provide a sanitized extract and the full copy via NDA link.

Target: can we have attachments ready by EOD Thu (2025-07-10)? If earlier, great.

Thanks — Alex

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 8 Jul 2025 11:20:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: encryption + KMS/HSM evidence for SIG/CAIQ sections

Alex / Marissa — quick status update.

- HSM attestation: I pulled the vendor attestation (VendorCrypt HSM attestation, issued 2025-06-15). It is a standard attestation PDF; it contains device serials and a few inventory lines. I'll produce a sanitized extract that removes device serials and any full key material references. File: hsm_attestation_2025-06.pdf (attached).

- KMS rotation events: I ran an export from the ops KMS for the tenant. Raw export contains UUIDs and actor email addresses — per policy we will pseudonymize. I prepared kms_rotation_extract_2025-07.csv with hashed key IDs and actor hashes, plus event types. I also included redaction_notes.txt describing the pseudonymization method (SHA256 of id + salt).

Notes on transit and TLS: we enforce TLS 1.2+ with forward secrecy and our load balancers terminate TLS using a standard cipher list (ECDHE AES-GCM). I'll draft the precise cipher suite list and include it in the CAIQ snippet.

One operational caveat: the raw KMS export contains internal service principals performing automated rotations; we will group those under a single actor_hash labeled "automation_janitor" to avoid exposing tool names. Confirm if Aurora needs the original service principal names; if so, we can provide via NDA.

Attaching: hsm_attestation_2025-06.pdf; kms_rotation_extract_2025-07.csv; redaction_notes.txt

Irene
Irene Choi | Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Request: encryption + KMS/HSM evidence for SIG/CAIQ sections

Tom — thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a preliminary package for your review: a sanitized HSM attestation extract, a KMS rotation CSV with hashed key IDs and actor pseudonyms, and a short notes file that documents the redaction approach. We also included a one-page CAIQ/SIG snippet describing envelope encryption, key wrapping (KEK hierarchy), and our emergency rotation playbook.

Attachments (attached to this email):
- redwood-sig-response-20250708.pdf (CAIQ/SIG snippet + short statement)
- hsm_attestation_2025-06.pdf (sanitized extract)
- kms_rotation_extract_2025-07.csv (sanitized rotation events)
- redaction_notes.txt

Key points:
- No raw key material or PKCS#11 traces are included.
- Key IDs are hashed with a salt (SHA256) and actor identifiers are pseudonymized. The CSV preserves timestamps and rotation event types so you can validate periodic rotation cadence.
- Transit: TLS 1.2+ with ECDHE and AES-GCM; we will include exact cipher suites in the full CAIQ deliverable if needed.
- HSM: vendor attestation scope covers tenancy isolation and tamper-evident controls; full vendor report is available under NDA if you need device serials.

If the sanitized extracts meet Aurora's needs, we can finalize the package for upload to your secure SFTP or a gated Drive link. If you need any of the redactions reversed for an in-person review under an NDA, we can accommodate that process.

Drive link (read-only): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AbCExampleSharedEvidence

Please confirm whether you want the final package delivered to the Drive link above or via a transfer (SFTP/secure Share). Also confirm whether the pseudonymization approach is acceptable.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
